about: LIN-3188: incidents of cross-session failure patterns on record in the tracker since 1 June (LIN-300 onward), hand-coded by the author from the candidates scripts/survey-hides-register.mjs --candidates finds (468), reading each title and the first ~1,500 characters of its description from the snapshot scripts/survey-hides-tracker.mjs takes, plus the 25 supervisor failures of wake-inventory-failures.json, the 2026-08-09 incident document and the 1 October circular wait named in LIN-3188. Kept: a ticket recording an instance of the failure happening (or, for P3, a test observed to pass only on retry); dropped: features, plans, measurements, and latent defects found only by reading code unless another paper's record already counts them. pattern: P1 healed/masked error, P2 circular/orphaned wait, P3 passes only on retry, P4 wake that changes nothing, P5 lost wake or lost input, P6 stalled/wedged session or runner, P7 duplicated work, P8 loop/runaway, P9 shared-state collision between concurrent sessions, P0 one of the 25 supervisor failures or a periodical failure that fits none of these. repo: where the fault lived ('both' when the fix or mechanism spans them). crossSession: true when no single session that hit it could see the failure as a pattern (it saw a retry succeed, a quiet wait, one red run), false when the session that hit it saw the whole failure. onset: the first occurrence the record states (UTC date), else null. filed: the ticket's createdAt (added by the summary from the fetched detail). detectedBy: who first recorded it, from the record's own words: person (John), flight-companion (FC or operator session), supervisor (an autopilot, coordinator, stepper or runner), agent-in-session (a worker that hit it in its own work, including a close-out's verification run), review (found reading code or measuring, in another ticket's research, review or a paper), periodical, code (a watchdog's own message), unknown. idleMinutes and occurrences only where the record states them; onset is a UTC timestamp where the record gives the time, else a date (read as 00:00Z, so time to discovery is then high by up to a day). The 1 October wait has no ticket and no timestamps; its 35 minutes to discovery is from LIN-3188's text (discoveredAfterMinutes).
